articleTitle: “An introduction to the discussion on domestic electricity”
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In introducing the theme “Domestic Electricity” I am faced with the fact that the subject is one of which every member of the audience has, in one way or another, a good knowledge. In using the term “Domestic Electricity” I really mean electricity in the home. It is my intention to keep to generalities, to give a résumé of the progress made in the use of electricity in the home over, say, the past ten years and not to enter into a highly controversial subject, such as the electricity tariff or the value of the domestic load to an electricity undertaking. These are subjects which have been discussed at length in all Municipal Electrical Engineers' Conventions.

articleTitle: A summary and discussion of some modern problems in internal combustion engineering
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: One of the first points to note in internal combustion motor operation, whether of the reciprocating or turbine type, is that we are dealing with a mechanism operated directly by forces developed by “explosion” or “combustion.” These two terms “explosion” and “combustion” provide the keys which are being used today to unlock the mysteries of the phenomenon known as “detonation.” Whatever may be the true explanation of this elusive characteristic in fuel reactions with air or oxygen, the reason for its annoying effects on internal combustion motor performance is clear enough. We know that to obtain sweet performance of any mechanism there must be conformity between the rate of application of the force applied at any instant and the velocity of the mechanism at that instant, otherwise much of the energy delivered will be dissipated in impact losses. The more rapid the application of the force and the slower the moving mechanism the greater will be the magnitude of that energy loss.
